organizations.normalization_notes: The personnel history names the employing unit as the U.S. Information Center, O.W.I.; that historical wording is preserved on the affiliation.
New York and Beverly Hills positions remain distinct affiliation records under the same historical company.
The personnel file says the magazine folded; no successor organization is inferred.

organizations.canonical_name: Fourth Interceptor Command, Aircraft Warning Service
organizations.historical_name: Aircraft Warning Service, U.S. Army Interceptor Command
organizations.normalization_notes: The file describes unpaid Aircraft Warning Service work under the Fourth Interceptor Command; it is recorded as volunteer service, not civilian employment.

affiliations.research_notes: Her personnel history says she requested transfer to OSS from this position; an OSS oath in the same file is dated November 18, 1942.
This was the last paid private-sector employer listed before Red Cross, Aircraft Warning Service, OWI, and OSS work.
The application lists no salary and describes supervision of volunteer stenographic services; it is not treated as employment.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: Aircraft Warning Service, U.S. Army Interceptor Command
affiliations.date_precision: month; source conflict on exact start day
affiliations.research_notes: Two forms in the same personnel file give February 23 and March 8, 1942 as the start date. Both give June 1, 1942 as the end date and list no salary.

affiliations.date_precision: day for start; year for end
affiliations.research_notes: Two forms in the file call the role editor and correspondent and give May 1 and June 1, 1939 as the end date. The disagreement is preserved.
The personnel history says she left because of illness in her family and returned home.
The file records a B.A. in 1934. Smith College is classified as education, not an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Julia C. McWilliams is confirmed as the person later known as Julia Child.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The complete official personnel file uses the indexed maiden name and explicitly supplies the later surname Child.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact indexed full name, direct personnel-file linkage, matching OSS index context, and an explicit documented name variant.
claims.temporal_assessment: The file is a contemporaneous OSS personnel record with later archival identification of the surname Child.
claims.match_notes: The file is a direct identity source; no inference from fame or a namesake biography is used.

claims.claim_text: McWilliams’s immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the U.S. Information Center in the Office of War Information, where she served as a senior typist.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Reason for leaving: typed over 10,000 little white cards and put in for a transfer to OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Her dated personnel history identifies OWI work through November 16, 1942 and explicitly says she requested transfer to OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the indexed person’s complete personnel file.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate; an OSS oath in the same file is dated November 18, 1942.
claims.match_notes: OWI is classified as a government assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: McWilliams’s last documented civilian employer before wartime volunteer and government service was W. & J. Sloane in Beverly Hills.
claims.evidence_excerpt: W. & J. Sloane ... Beverly Hills, Calif ... Advertising Manager
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The experience record dates this private-sector advertising job from March 1 to July 1, 1941, before later volunteer and federal roles.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the indexed person’s complete personnel file.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit dates establish it as the last paid private-sector job listed before wartime service affiliations.
claims.match_notes: The later Red Cross and Aircraft Warning Service entries were unpaid volunteer roles; OWI was a federal assignment.

claims.claim_text: McWilliams supervised volunteer stenographic services for the American Red Cross’s Pasadena Chapter from October 1941 to June 1942.
claims.evidence_excerpt: AMERICAN RED CROSS: Pasadena Chapter. 10/1/41 to 6/1/42
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Two personnel-history entries agree on the organization, volunteer duties, and dates.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the indexed person’s complete personnel file.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly dated before OWI and OSS service.
claims.match_notes: This is published as volunteer service, not employment.

claims.claim_text: McWilliams performed unpaid plotter-filterer-clerk work for the Fourth Interceptor Command’s Aircraft Warning Service in 1942.
claims.evidence_excerpt: AIRCRAFT WARNING SERVICE, U. S. Army Interceptor Command, Los Angeles
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The personnel file identifies the organization, role, Los Angeles location, and June 1, 1942 end date.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the indexed person’s complete personnel file.
claims.temporal_assessment: Definitely pre-OSS, but two forms disagree on whether the work began February 23 or March 8, 1942.
claims.match_notes: The date disagreement is retained; the affiliation is classified as volunteer service because the application lists no salary.

claims.claim_text: McWilliams worked for The Coast Magazine as its Southern California fashion editor or correspondent beginning in November 1937.
claims.evidence_excerpt: THE COAST MAGAZINE, San Francisco, California ... Southern California Fashion Editor
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Two forms establish the magazine affiliation but differ slightly on the title and whether it ended in May or June 1939.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the indexed person’s complete personnel file.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar work; the exact 1939 end month remains conflicting.
claims.match_notes: The role-title and end-date variants are visible in the claim rather than silently normalized.

claims.claim_text: McWilliams worked at W. & J. Sloane in New York as assistant to the advertising manager from October 1935 to May 1937.
claims.evidence_excerpt: W. & J. SLOANE, 575 Fifth Avenue, New York City ... Assistant to Advertising Manager
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Her personnel history explicitly supplies the employer, role, location, and dates.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the indexed person’s complete personnel file.
claims.match_notes: This earlier New York position remains distinct from her later Beverly Hills advertising-manager job.

claims.claim_text: McWilliams graduated from Smith College with a B.A. in 1934.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Smith College, Northampton, Massachusetts. Graduated, B.A. 1934
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The personnel history documents the college, degree, and graduation year.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the indexed person’s complete personnel file.
claims.match_notes: Smith College is classified as student status and is not counted as an employer.

claims.claim_text: NARA’s complete digitized OSS personnel file for McWilliams, NAID 2180661, was reviewed for this profile.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 130-page public file is labeled complete and contains the personnel history and applications supporting the profile.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Direct file-unit linkage to the indexed exact name.
claims.temporal_assessment: Archival-status claim; not an employment chronology claim.
claims.match_notes: The profile preserves the index’s Box 513. NARA’s file introduction says Box 514, while the Catalog lists preservation Box 513A.
